newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. Asia official on visit to China.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. Asia official on visit to China.

text.p: The U.S. government's top Asia official, Winston Lord, is on a previously unannounced visit to China for talks expected to include human rights and alleged Chinese nuclear sales, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Lord, Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs, was preparing for a visit next month by Secretary of State Warren Christopher, but that "all issues are on the table".
Burns told a news briefing that Lord went to China after a visit last week to South Korea to discuss tensions over the beaching of a North Korean submarine on the South Korean coast last month.
Lord would also travel on to Japan, probably around Oct. 18 or 19, Burns said.

U.S. officials say relations with China have generally improved in recent months, but there have been frictions in the last two weeks over its treatment of dissidents and over fresh reports of Chinese nuclear sales to Pakistan.

"I think all issues are on the table in (Lord's) discussions with the Chinese. It wouldn't surprise me at all if that issue of the alleged sale of items between China and Pakistan came up," Burns said.

Nevertheless, he said Washington continued to maintain that China had not violated past pledges with the sale, which the Washington Times said last week consisted of a special industrial furnace and high-tech diagnostic equipment.

Burns added that human rights issues were also likely to be raised. The United States last week sharply criticised the sentencing of dissident Liu Xiaobo to three years in a labour camp, and apparent plans to try another dissenter, Wang Dan.
A third dissident, Wang Xizhe, is expected imminently in the United States after fleeing from China to Hong Kong.
Burns said Lord had considered the possibility of extending his trip beyond South Korea when he left Washington last week, but did not finally decide to do so until he was already in Asia.
Christopher is due to visit China Nov. 21-22 on a trip originally announced in July.
